newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana minister resigns over corruption accusations.
newsitem.headline: Ghana minister resigns over corruption accusations.

text.p: Ghana's Trade and Industry Minister Ibrahim Adam said on Friday that he had resigned to fight accusations of corruption levelled against him.
Adam told the state-run Ghana News Agency by telephone from his home in the northern town of Tamale that he had tendered his resignation to President Jerry Rawlings over a month ago.
State television said later Rawlings had accepted his resignation along with that of Isaac Adjei-Maafo, Presidential Staffer for Cocoa Affairs.

Adam said he wanted to redeem his good name after a report by the Commission for Human Rights and Administrative Justice made allegations against him. The television said Adjei-Maafo, also targeted in the report, wanted to do the same.
There was no immediate word on Adam's replacement.

The commission recommended he be sanctioned for waiving tax on fish for certain companies contrary to the Merchant Shipping Act. It spoke of "gross negligence of duty which has occasioned loss of billions of cedis in revenue to the state."
Adam, who is fighting for the Tamale seat in parliament in the December 7 general election, said he intended to appeal aginst the commission report, accusing it of ignoring expert evidence.
Emmanuel Osei-Owusu resigned as interior minister last month after the commission criticised him. Rawlings himself is standing for reelection on December 7.
